newsitem.title: USA: Massachusetts in Harvard Pilgrim probe - report.
newsitem.headline: Massachusetts in Harvard Pilgrim probe - report.

text.p: The Massachusetts attorney general is investigating the state's largest health maintenance organization for possible antitrust violations, the Boston Globe reported on Thursday.

Assistant Attorney General Barbara Anthony told the newspaper that the probe began last month after New England Medical Center in Boston launched a high-profile campaign to pressure Harvard Pilgrim Health Care to do business with the hospital. The medical center, the teaching hospital for Tufts University School of Medicine, alleged it was unfair for the HMO to sent its patients to every major teaching hospital in the area except New England Medical, the newspaper said.
Harvard Pilgrim has over one million subscribers and a contract wih the HMO could be lucrative for the center, which is burdened by a $240 million debt, the Globe reported.

"We were contacted several weeks ago by the attorney general's office, and we've been in regular communication with them since," Harvard Pilgrim spokeswoman Patti Embry-Tautenhan told The Globe. "We cooperated fully with their request."
Neither the attorney general's office nor Harvard Pilgrim could be immediately reached for comment.
